title: issues verbs act only on the working directory's project, so filing into another registered project means cd-ing into it first: add intent issues --project <project>
body: Requested by hv on 2026-09-28, raised from a Lamplight session: filing this issue and the one before it meant cd-ing into Intent first, because every `intent issues` verb takes its project from the working directory (Project::discover walks up from the start directory, intentsvcs/src/project.rs:1561), and no flag or environment variable names another one. Proposal: `intent issues --project <project> add <title> ...`, and the same for the other issues verbs (`new` is already `add`'s alias), acts on a project from the machine's registry, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/intent/projects.json, instead of the project the working directory is in. The registry lists roots and nothing else (intentsvcs/src/projects.rs:1-13), so `<project>` would resolve by reading each registered root's own intent/.config/config.json: its `project_id`, its `project_name` (case-insensitive), or the registered root path itself. A value that matches more than one project is refused, naming each candidate; a value that matches none is refused, listing the registered projects. It never falls back to the working directory's project, because that would file the issue in the wrong estate without saying so. The write goes through the target project's store exactly as a run from inside that project would, so its event, canon file and view land in that project's tree, and the answer names the project and its root so the caller can see where the issue went. Design question to settle first: whether --project belongs to `issues` alone, or is a global flag that every project-scoped verb honours (st, wp, ac, wb and the rest), with issues as its first user.
